outcome: Presence of contrast avid lesions with high SUV on F-18 FDG PET/CT scans
Difficulty in differentiating benign glial tissue from residual/recurrent malignant lesions based on imaging
Confirmation of benign glial tissue via biopsy
cohort: A single patient diagnosed with immature teratoma of the ovary who developed gliomatosis peritonei during follow-up after primary surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy.
finding: Gliomatosis peritonei lesions appear as contrast-avid lesions with high SUV on F-18 FDG PET/CT scans, making differentiation from malignant lesions difficult without biopsy.
